author: /root/back_cvs_sources
scope: Independent educational content review of the final 94-question back, spinal-cord and thoracic/CVS anatomy expansion, its 22 concept records, objective/module/coverage links, source-audit metadata and four original-source figure assets. Not a claim of medical licensure or official lecture/exam alignment.

reviewBasis.content: Read all 94 stems, keyed answers and all distractor explanations, then reconciled the frozen final export with the authoring overrides. Checked concepts, retrieval answers and objective references against the final questions.
reviewBasis.sources: Checked cited local Gray's Anatomy for Students 3rd-edition page/OCR evidence and Gray's Anatomy 42nd-edition excerpts. Independently inspected the relevant full passages for high-risk laterality, spinal-cord termination/clinical patterns, canal boundaries, spinal vascular territories, cardiac valves/conduction/vessels, mediastinal and diaphragm relationships. Page locators distinguish printed and local PDF pages.
reviewBasis.figures: Visually inspected all four staged PNGs and their figure-manifest source-page/crop locators; verified applied question placement. Anatomical labels are intentionally retained, but the keyed answer requires applying boundary, meningeal-space, canal-compartment or feeder-dependence relationships rather than naming a displayed label.
reviewBasis.structural: Ran reviewer_validate.mjs after final changes: no validation errors; 94 questions, 22 concepts, 7 modules, 22 coverage entries and 165 source-audit entries. All 94 retrieval answers exactly match the keyed answer plus explanation.

changes.change: Replaced loss of disc height with an explicitly foraminal posterolateral disc bulge, so the anterior-versus-posterior boundary comparison follows the described lesions without conflating vertical pedicle approximation. Clarified explanation and synchronized concept key point/retrieval prompt/answer.
Clarified that disc protrusion comes from the anterior canal boundary; synchronized concept key point and retrieval answer.
Conservatively lowered difficulty 4 to 3 for items resolved principally through one established anatomical fact or standard one-step relation. No answer keys changed.
Changed media paths to relative term2/cvs/comprehensive/<basename> for the documented app import contract. Figure bytes unchanged.
Replaced independent-review-pending quality flag with independent-content-reviewed. Kept question status draft for the parent integrator's signed-gate promotion.

highRiskChecks: Back 044 now cites Gray42 printed p. 822 rather than 824; valveless vertebral venous communication is supported.
Back 048 uses interspinales attachment/span recognition and avoids an incorrect uniform posterior-ramus rule for intertransversarii.
Back 046 specifies trunk rotation when contrasting transversospinales and splenius, avoiding a semispinalis-capitis laterality ambiguity in the underlying source.

Cord termination is expressed as a typical teaching level, with source variability not treated as an invariant; conus/cauda clinical comparison is a localization tendency rather than a diagnostic rule.
Thoracic coronary dominance is tied to posterior interventricular supply; mitral papillary support of both leaflets and AV-conduction relationships agree with the cited local source passages.
Question 038 explicitly distinguishes the figure's cord-containing level from the lower lumbar-cistern scenario.

difficultySummary.note: Difficulty is an unpiloted content judgment, not an empirically measured item statistic. This reviewed batch does not independently meet a 50% difficulty-4/5 target; grades were not inflated to satisfy that ratio.

limitations: Book-extension status is retained. Official lecture coverage and exam weighting are not certified.
Existing-question IDs in the source audit document mapping and do not newly certify the legacy bank's answer/source quality.
This is a bounded anatomy expansion, not whole-neurocourse coverage or proof that every source topic has an active question.
Original local book figures are retained for the user's study context; this review does not certify public redistribution rights.

modalityVerification.note: Publication/modality follow-up confirmed all four figure-backed questions already use image_single_best_answer in the signed staging payload. No question or gate bytes were changed; prompts, options, keys, sources and images remain exactly as reviewed.
